These TLS details concern the HTTPS measurement endpoint inside the selected tunnel. A failed measurement alone does not prove the candidate Address is unusable.

Controls use the same running tunnel. The HTTP/1.1 control checks one 1 KB response; the native control checks HTTPS status. Controls do not count as successful scan samples.

Three native Xray Real Delay samples using the same builder and configured URL as Profiles; each sample is the best of two internal attempts. Classic Mux and custom DNS/routing are excluded by that latency builder. Variation is not packet loss or network jitter. The optional 10 MB download is a separate result.

With the 10 MB download off, three sequential baseline controls add up to six requests to the configured test URL. Controls do not qualify IPs. Order and network variation can affect the comparison. Keep the VPN off.
Direct IPv4 edge scan: TCP 80, TCP 443 and verified TLS. Stop the VPN. The profile supplies only provider identification and SNI; no tunnel or download is started.
Choose a profile with an Address belonging to a known CDN and a valid DNS SNI. Credentials and transport are not tested.

Reachable means TCP 80 or 443 connected. TLS certificate and hostname verification are separate. One sample per stage; times are not tunnel latency or download speed. Test your configuration manually.
Provider %1$s · Up to %2$d IPv4 edges. Per IP: TCP 80, TCP 443, then verified TLS if 443 connects. No HTTP or file download. Keep the VPN off and network unchanged. Deadline: 30 minutes.
